Forest Plot for brma Objects Using metafor

Source: R/forest.R
forest.Rd

metafor::forest() creates a forest plot for a fitted brma object by adapting RoBMA results to metafor's public forest plotting API. Study rows are drawn by forest.default and the RoBMA pooled posterior summary is added with addpoly.default.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'brma'
forest(
  x,
  addfit = TRUE,
  addpred = FALSE,
  newdata = NULL,
  predstyle = "line",
  mlab = NULL,
  row = -1,
  level = 95,
  bias_adjusted = TRUE,
  conditional = FALSE,
  as_data = FALSE,
  predlim,
  border,
  constarea,
  ...
)

# S3 method for class 'metafor_forest.brma'
forest(
  x,
  addfit = TRUE,
  predstyle = "line",
  mlab = NULL,
  row = -1,
  predlim,
  border,
  constarea,
  ...
)

Arguments

x

a fitted brma object or an object returned by as_metafor_forest().

addfit

logical; whether to add the RoBMA pooled-effect summary polygon. Defaults to TRUE.

addpred

logical; whether to add a posterior prediction interval for one new true effect. Defaults to FALSE.

newdata

optional one-row prediction design used when addpred = TRUE. See as_metafor_forest().

predstyle

character; prediction interval style passed to addpoly.default. Defaults to "line".

mlab

label for the summary row. Defaults to "Pooled Effect" for a pooled summary and "Predicted Effect" when newdata requests a moderator-specific prediction.

row

numeric row position for the pooled-effect summary polygon. Defaults to -1.

level

credible/confidence level in percent, greater than 0 and less than 100. A value below 1 is read as a proportion (0.95 is 95 percent), so 1 means 1 percent. Defaults to 95.

bias_adjusted

logical; whether pooled and prediction summaries should adjust for publication bias. Defaults to TRUE.

conditional

logical; whether to return conditional posterior summaries for RoBMA product-space objects. Defaults to FALSE.

as_data

logical; if TRUE, returns the prepared data instead of creating a plot.

predlim

argument passed to addpoly.default for prediction interval rendering.

border, constarea

arguments passed to addpoly.default for summary polygon rendering.

...

additional arguments passed to forest.default. This includes auxiliary-column arguments such as ilab, ilab.lab, ilab.xpos, and ilab.pos. Shared graphical arguments such as annotate, digits, transf, atransf, efac, col, lty, fonts, and cex are also forwarded to addpoly.default.

Value

Invisibly returns the object returned by forest.default. If as_data = TRUE, returns a metafor_forest.brma object.

Details

This method deliberately uses metafor's public vector-based forest plotting API instead of constructing a fake metafor model object. The observed study rows are shown as usual Wald intervals based on the supplied effect sizes and standard errors. The model summary row uses the posterior mean and credible interval from pooled_effect. When addpred = TRUE without newdata, the displayed center, credible interval, and marginal prediction interval use the average-design target returned by pooled_effect. With explicit newdata, all three refer to that one prediction row and the prediction interval uses predict.brma with type = "estimate" and conditioning_depth = "marginal". For metafor's predstyle = "shade" and predstyle = "dist", the adapter supplies the predictive density. Without newdata it is the posterior predictive density, a normal mixture over the posterior draws, smoothed by a normal kernel for display (a kernel density estimate of predictive draws without their simulation noise); the smoothing keeps point masses (draws without heterogeneity) visible. With newdata it is a kernel density estimate of the predictive draws from predict.brma. The displayed prediction-interval endpoints are the quantiles reported by pooled_effect or predict.brma.

Additional study-level columns can be added with metafor's ilab interface. When supplied to as_metafor_forest() or to metafor::forest(..., as_data = TRUE), those arguments are stored in the adapter object's forest_args; presentation options such as addfit, row, and predstyle are retained by forest(..., as_data = TRUE) for later rendering. Explicit plot-time arguments override stored defaults. When supplied to metafor::forest() at plot time, they are forwarded directly.

Use as_metafor_forest() to prepare the adapter object without requiring a metafor installation.

See also

as_metafor_forest(), pooled_effect(), predict.brma()

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
if (requireNamespace("metadat", quietly = TRUE) &&
    requireNamespace("metafor", quietly = TRUE)) {
  data(dat.bcg, package = "metadat")
  dat <- metafor::escalc(
    measure = "RR",
    ai      = tpos,
    bi      = tneg,
    ci      = cpos,
    di      = cneg,
    data    = dat.bcg
  )

  fit <- brma(yi = yi, vi = vi, data = dat, measure = "RR")
  metafor::forest(fit)
  metafor::forest(fit, addpred = TRUE, atransf = exp)

  count_columns <- as.matrix(dat[, c("tpos", "tneg", "cpos", "cneg")])
  metafor::forest(
    fit,
    addpred   = TRUE,
    slab      = paste(dat$author, dat$year),
    ilab      = count_columns,
    ilab.lab  = c("T+", "T-", "C+", "C-"),
    ilab.xpos = c(-8.5, -7.5, -6.5, -5.5),
    xlim      = c(-10, 4),
    atransf   = exp
  )
}
} # }
